quickAnswer: Cleaning an 18,000 sq ft multi-department office wing with 5 restrooms costs $1,272 to $2,202 per visit on a 3x/week schedule ($16,536 to $28,626 per month) or $1,209 to $2,094 per visit for 5x/week weekday service ($26,175 to $45,335 per month). Pricing uses the 10,000–24,999 sq ft bracket ($0.07 to $0.12/sq ft) plus $75 to $150 per visit in restroom surcharges across 5.25 to 7.68 ISSA labor hours.

blocks.text: An **18,000 sq ft multi-department office wing** sits squarely in the mid-large commercial tier (**10,000–24,999 sq ft at $0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft**), yet its operational footprint behaves differently from an open single-tenant studio. Departments such as sales, finance, engineering, and HR typically split the floor plate into badge-restricted zones, multiple copy-and-mail alcoves, and **5 separate restrooms** positioned along opposite wings.

Because custodians must cross longer corridors, manage color-coded microfiber tools to prevent restroom-to-breakroom cross-contamination, and unlock separate departmental suites, labor allocation climbs to **5.25 to 7.68 hours per visit**. Below is the exact mathematical breakdown from our [Office Cleaning Cost Guides](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/) benchmark engine so you can verify vendor bids before locking in an annual budget.
18,000 Sq Ft Cleaning Cost by Service Frequency (5 Restrooms)

At **18,000 sq ft** on commercial carpet (**1.00x multiplier**) at the **1.00x US national average**, base square-footage labor combines with **$75 to $150 per visit** for **5 restrooms** ($15 to $30 each). Notice how monthly cadence (**1.28x**) inflates per-visit labor to **$1,688–$2,915** due to accumulated soil, whereas **3x/week (0.95x)** lowers the per-visit charge to **$1,272–$2,202** across **13.00 visits per month** and **5x/week (0.90x)** brings each visit down to **$1,209–$2,094** across **21.65 visits per month**.

blocks.text: Flooring Mix and Multi-Wing Scope Add-Ons

Multi-department wings almost never use one continuous floor finish. Reception and client-facing boardrooms often run **engineered hardwood (1.08x)** or **ceramic tile (1.12x)**, main circulation spines use **polished concrete (0.95x)** or **VCT/LVT vinyl (1.04x)**, and departmental workstation pods sit on **carpet tiles (1.00x)**. Switching from pure carpet to a **Mixed (1.05x)** scope on a 3x/week schedule increases the monthly budget from **$16,536–$28,626** to **$17,314–$29,960**.

Add-ons also scale differently across 18,000 sq ft. While **breakroom sanitation** (**+$12 to $25/visit**) and **interior glass partitions** (**+$15 to $35/visit**) remain modest fixed per-visit line items, **vendor-supplied paper and soap consumables** (**$0.012 to $0.025/sq ft/visit**) add **$216 to $450 every visit** (**$2,808 to $5,850 per month** at 3x/week), and **amortized quarterly deep floor care** (**$0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month**) adds **$540 to $1,080 per month**.

blocks.title: Use Zone-Tiered Frequency to Trim 15% Without Cutting Restroom Hygiene
blocks.text: In an 18,000 sq ft multi-department layout, ask bidders to price restrooms, breakrooms, and lobby corridors at 5x/week while dropping low-traffic archive or engineering pods to 2x/week vacuuming. Departmental zone tiering preserves daily sanitation where traffic concentrates without paying 5x/week floor labor across empty rooms.
Crew Allocation, Hourly Benchmarks, and Corridor Tool Workflow

At ISSA commercial production averages (**2,800 to 4,000 sq ft/hr** plus **0.15 to 0.25 hrs per restroom**), servicing 18,000 sq ft and 5 restrooms requires **5.25 to 7.68 labor hours per visit**. Most regional contractors assign a **two-person team for 2.75 to 3.85 hours** or a **three-person team for 1.8 to 2.5 hours**, splitting specialist roles so one technician handles all five restrooms and breakrooms while the partner vacuums and dust-mops departmental wings.

Standard daytime porter or supplemental labor runs **$35 to $65 per hour**, while specialized post-construction HEPA cleaning, biohazard remediation, or high-speed wood/stone buffing runs **$55 to $95 per hour**. If your wing features hardwood corridors or conference suites, review machine compatibility in our guide to the [best hardwood-safe commercial floor polishers](/commercial-vacuums-and-floor-machines/best-hardwood-safe-commercial-floor-polishers/) before approving a vendor's machine list.

**Balanced Absorbency Damp Mopping:** The **Rubbermaid Commercial Super Stitch Blend Mop Head 24-oz** uses a launderable **cotton-synthetic blend** engineered for medium-duty soil release in departmental breakrooms and tile entries.

blocks.title: Badge Security, Keyholder Bonding, and 1099 Subcontractor Risks
blocks.text: Multi-department wings with HR, finance, or R&D suites require strict access governance. Confirm your vendor employs W-2 cleaners covered by Workers' Compensation, carries a janitorial surety bond for after-hours keycard access, and prohibits unauthorized 1099 subcontracting in writing.
Step-by-Step Bid Normalization Across 18,000–30,000 Sq Ft Proposals

If your company occupies an 18,000 sq ft wing today—or is evaluating expansion into [20,000 sq ft](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/cost-to-clean-a-20000-sq-ft-office/), [25,000 sq ft](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/cost-to-clean-a-25000-sq-ft-office/), or [30,000 sq ft](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/cost-to-clean-a-30000-sq-ft-office/) footprints—standardize every bid with these steps:

items.name: Map Exact Restroom and Breakroom Counts by Wing
items.text: Verify whether each wing restroom has two stalls or six fixtures; high-fixture multi-stall restrooms justify the upper $25–$30 per-restroom surcharge.

items.name: Normalize Monthly Bids to 4.333 Weeks
items.text: Divide proposed monthly retainers by 13.00 (3x/week) or 21.65 (5x/week) to expose disguised per-visit rate hikes or fifth-week exclusions.

items.name: Audit Implied Labor Hours Against ISSA Standards
items.text: Confirm the bid supports 5.25 to 7.68 labor hours per visit; ultra-cheap quotes imply skipped dusting, unwashed mop heads, or illegal labor classification.

items.name: Enforce Color-Coded Microfiber and SDS Closets
items.text: Mandate separate mop/cloth colors for restrooms versus kitchenettes and keep laminated OSHA HazCom Safety Data Sheets in every wing closet.

faqs.q: Why does 18,000 sq ft still use the $0.07–$0.12/sq ft bracket instead of the $0.05–$0.10 tier?
faqs.a: In standard commercial estimating, the enterprise tier ($0.05–$0.10 per sq ft) begins at 25,000 sq ft. Suites between 10,000 and 24,999 sq ft fall into the $0.07–$0.12/sq ft bracket because multi-department partition walls, five separate restrooms, and dispersed trash stations prevent the linear auto-scrubber speeds seen in larger open campuses.

faqs.q: How does the 4.333 weeks-per-month rule affect a 5x/week 18,000 sq ft invoice?
faqs.a: Five weekdays per week across a 52-week year equals 260 annual visits, or 21.65 visits per month (using 4.333 weeks/month, rounded to 4.33 in our calculator). Multiplying $1,209–$2,094 per visit by 21.65 produces the true flat monthly budget of $26,175 to $45,335 without surprise fifth-week add-on bills.

faqs.q: What Certificates of Insurance (COI) should cover a multi-department office wing?
faqs.a: Require $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate Commercial General Liability naming both tenant and building owner as Additional Insured, statutory Workers' Compensation for all W-2 cleaners, and a commercial dishonesty/fidelity bond covering keycards and sensitive departmental workspaces.

faqs.q: What OSHA compliance rules apply to janitorial closets inside an 18,000 sq ft office?
faqs.a: OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200) requires secondary spray bottles to display chemical hazard labels and Safety Data Sheets (SDS) to remain accessible on site. Any cleanup involving blood or bodily fluids falls under OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) and typically bills at $55 to $95 per specialty hour.

faqs.q: Are Green Seal GS-37 products worth requiring for multi-wing offices?
faqs.a: Yes. Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice concentrates eliminate harsh ammonia and quaternary-residue odors across enclosed departmental pods while typically adding 0% to 4% to contract pricing when paired with closed-loop dilution stations.
